findings.reason: naming the enumerator turns §11's script into a reader of existing machinery and removes a second cross-project glob whose path resolution would otherwise drift from the store's.
findings.text: the census in §11 is specified as a fresh walk of "`plan-*.vN.json` across every project" with no citation of `list_plan_reviews` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:516`), the function that already enumerates every project's plan reviews, sets each record's `project` and `review_path`, and restricts the glob so code reviews are never mixed in

findings.reason: §10 should name `_is_review_node` as the owner and make dispatch's recogniser call it, so the one plan-review identity has one recogniser as well as one constant.
findings.text: `_is_review_run` here recognises a review by `role == "review"` or `RECORD_NODE_ID.startswith(REVIEW_NODE_PREFIX)` independently of `reckon/crew/recovery.py:904` `_is_review_run`, which delegates to the owning `_is_review_node` (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:228`); since `"plan-review-of-…".startswith("review-of-")` is false, the two predicates disagree on a plan-review node whose role is not exactly `review`, and §10 — which names only "dispatch's reader" and the literal — does not consolidate them

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the remaining nodes consolidate rather than spread: §9 moves the report grammar into `reckon/crew/review.py` beside `parse_review`, §10 reduces the plan-review node identity to one constant; neither adds a wrapper over the same machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:11187` re-implements the review-run recogniser that `reckon/crew/recovery.py:228` (`_is_review_node`) already owns; §10 fixes only the literal, leaving two predicates that can disagree about a plan-review node.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §11's census proposes enumerating "every stored plan review ... (`plan-*.vN.json` across every project)" without citing `list_plan_reviews` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:516`), which already performs exactly that cross-project walk.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §9 extends the existing parser owner (`reckon/crew/review.py:409`, `_FIND_RE` at :380) instead of layering a parallel parser, and §3's design review extends the build skill's existing reuse-map rule (`skills/reckon-build/references/sprint-orchestration.md:713`) rather than adding a second reuse mechanism.
